text: The Patriots pulled off a stunning Week 4 comeback against the Bills, with Drake Maye orchestrating a 29-26 victory at Highmark Stadium that earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for his three-touchdown performance—a clutch rebound that head coach Mike Vrabel emphasized as critical for the defending AFC champions' season trajectory. Now sitting at 2-2 after what some are already calling a season-saving rally, New England faces a Las Vegas Raiders squad at Gillette Stadium this Sunday at 1 PM ET, though the Patriots will have to navigate a pressing concern in the backfield, where Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with an injury that leaves the running back position clouded heading into Week 5. The Raiders present a formidable receiving challenge, with their 1-2 tight end combo of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer looming after the Patriots successfully neutralized Buffalo's Dalton Kincaid the previous week—a stark contrast in what will be a test of whether New England's defensive adjustments can travel. Whether the Patriots' dramatic comeback represents a genuine reset or another overreaction will likely be answered by how they handle this Raiders matchup, with injury reports and Mike Vrabel's latest press conference providing the framework for understanding where the team actually stands.
